H_hierarchical.evidence: The control architecture explicitly layers global navigation, local navigation, and lower gait sub-behavior FSMs; SmoveFwd/SmoveLeft/SmoveRight are refined by Stripod/Swave/Send sub-FSMs.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Transitions use sensor/status guards for obstacle, heading error, waypoint, fault, and corridor predicates; SmoveLeft to SmoveRight fires on fleftobs OR foutofcorridor, with corridor checked from GPS plus odometry.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: States set up repositories, request or dispatch waypoints, prepare status messages, generate body and gait trajectories, notify the user, and resume/suspend gait submachines via OnEntry/OnExit/Internal actions.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: ffault guards global termination, local stop, and sub-behavior termination; Sstop halts the robot and returns it to its initial configuration.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: SmoveLeft information is split across the Local navigation FSM state list, State activities guard discussion, Implementation OnEntry/OnExit prose, and Simulation traces.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as gait, blocked path, and fault are accompanied by explicit transition targets or actions, so no extra transition rule must be decoded from outside domain knowledge.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Parent-state actions such as resuming BehaviourGaitLeft on entry and suspending it on exit appear in implementation prose rather than in the original local-state definitions.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: SmoveLeft to SmoveRight uses a boolean OR of fleftobs and foutofcorridor; foutofcorridor is derived from GPS plus local odometry and corridor bounds.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: Motion states have parent-level entry/internal/exit behavior while their lower gait submachines choose Stripod or Swave.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: The same ffault condition routes the global FSM to Send, the local FSM to Sstop, and the gait FSM to Send, forming a cross-layer escape rule.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: The sample has shallow composite motion states that resume a gait sub-FSM; the terrain-dependent gait selection is nontrivial but only one nested layer is described.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The guard set includes obstacle/no-obstacle complements, heading-left/right/no-heading conditions, corridor checks from combined sensors, fault-vector status, and OR composition.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: ffault is a cross-layer escape, and Internal sections encode repeated per-mode monitoring/actions that would be compact as forced/aspect rules.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Outputs are abstracted through status, waypoint, demand repositories, and user notifications; the same action structure can target simulator or hardware interfaces.

key_nl_quotes: This two-tier description follows the concept of hierarchical FSMs.

one_line_pitch: A layered walking-machine supervisor stresses hierarchy, guard attribution, action placement, and cross-layer fault exits in one concrete robotic control case.
rationale: The paper gives enough concrete structure to build a reference HSM: named global/local/gait states, guard predicates, action sections, and fault endpoints are all specified. It is a strong baseline trap because key action and guard facts are distributed across state descriptions, state-activity prose, implementation details, and simulation traces. No hard exclusion is triggered because the benchmarkable target is the hierarchical supervisor, with FSM execution serialized by a scheduler rather than requiring orthogonal statechart regions.
